Superconducting Diode Effect.title: Superconducting Diode Effect due to the Inverse Spin Hall Effect in Josephson Junctions with Extrinsic Spin-Orbit Interaction
Superconducting Diode Effect.authors: Yositake Takane, Aurélien Manchon, Gen Tatara
Superconducting Diode Effect.abstract: The spin density and Josephson current at equilibrium are studied numerically in a superconductor-normal metal-superconductor (SNS) junction with extrinsic spin-orbit interaction in the N segment. This system preserves structural inversion symmetry. We find that the Josephson current generates the spin Hall effect, resulting in an opposite spin density near the two edges of the N segment. We also find that a Zeeman magnetic field with gradient applied to the N segment generates an anomalous phase shift due to the inverse spin Hall effect, resulting in a diode effect when higher harmonics of the Josephson current are present. These results are consistent with those of a previous theoretical study based on diagrammatic perturbation theory. We find that the diode effect becomes more pronounced when stronger coupling between the N and S segments enhances the higher harmonics.

Turning a superconducting diode into a Feynman ratchet to realize a nanoscale heat engine
Superconducting Diode Effect.authors: Konstantinos Kontogeorgiou, İnanç Adagideli, Géraldine Haack, Fabian Hassler
Superconducting Diode Effect.abstract: Feynman's ratchet illustrates how work can be extracted from thermal fluctuations in the presence of two heat baths at different temperatures. While some experimental realizations of the ratchet effect have been studied, most lack miniaturization, which is important for some applications. Here, we propose a physical implementation of Feynman's ratchet based on Josephson junctions exhibiting the superconducting diode effect. This setup functions as a heat engine that generates work solely from a temperature gradient via thermal fluctuations. We analyze its output power and efficiency, and, through the Seebeck coefficient, identify the conditions under which the device operates in reverse, functioning instead as a Peltier cooler.

Superconducting Diode Effect.title: Twisted superconducting quantum diodes for high fidelity anharmonic qubits
Superconducting Diode Effect.authors: Han Zhong, Denis Kochan, Igor Žutić, Yingying Wu
Superconducting Diode Effect.abstract: Abstract In superconducting circuits, bidirectional signal propagation can cause back-reflections and back-action that couple environmental noise back to coherent elements, degrading fidelity. Nonreciprocal superconducting diodes provide an intrinsic route to suppress such back-scattering at the circuit level. However, their diode efficiency and quantum integration remain limited. Here, we realize a quantum diode in twisted NbSe 2 under in-plane and out-of-plane magnetic fields. A mere 1 ∘ twist yields an efficiency enhancement over pristine devices, reaching 27.6%. Quantum simulations reveal that this intermediate efficiency, well below 100% ideal, is both experimentally practical and optimal for preserving qubit anharmonicity and stabilizing two-level systems. These findings show that maximal rectification is not always beneficial for quantum information, establishing a new principle for designing the fundamental properties of twisted superconductors towards low-power, high-fidelity quantum circuits.

Superconducting Diode Effect.title: High-Efficiency Field-Free Superconducting Diodes in Mo$_2$N/FePt Bilayers
Superconducting Diode Effect.authors: Juan S. Cruz, Emilio De Biasi, Juan C. Zapata, Yeonkyu Lee, Jeehoon Kim, Nestor Haberkorn
Superconducting Diode Effect.abstract: Near-ideal, field-free superconducting diode behavior is demonstrated in room-temperature-grown Mo$_2$N/FePt bilayers. The response is consistent with remanent FePt stripe domains producing polarity-dependent thresholds for flux entry and vortex motion. Micromagnetic simulations reveal a periodic stray-field modulation across the stripes and asymmetric field enhancement near their ends at the bridge edges. One current polarity remains nearly dissipationless up to a sizable fraction of the estimated depairing current, whereas the opposite polarity develops dissipation at much lower current, yielding diode efficiencies up to approximately 85% in the thinner bilayer. The nonreciprocity can be continuously tuned by the in-plane magnetic preparation angle and reversibly switched by reverse-field excursions through the hysteretic reversal of the FePt layer. These results support edge-controlled flux entry and vortex motion as a route to high-efficiency superconducting diodes.

Superconducting Diode Effect.title: High-Efficiency and Large Supercurrent Rectification with Superconducting Coil
Superconducting Diode Effect.authors: Takumi Ichikawa, Daisuke Takegami, Gen Nishijima, Shunsuke Kawakami, Tsutomu Nojima, Yuji Tsuchiya, Satoshi Awaji, Fuyuki Ando, Ken-ichi Uchida, Yuya Hattori, Yoshikazu Mizuguchi
Superconducting Diode Effect.abstract: Superconducting diodes (SDs) are devices that rectify supercurrent through the difference in the superconducting critical current (Ic) between forward and reverse current directions. For bringing such SDs closer to practical superconducting power electronics applications, a combination of both high rectification efficiency (η) and a large Ic difference (ΔIc) is required. Here, we propose and demonstrate a coil-shaped superconducting wire device concept to induce a large SD effect, arising from the compensation between an external magnetic field (Hext) and the field generated by the coil itself. From transport Ic measurements on coil-shaped SDs based on a Sn10-Pb90 solder wire, we achieved a η of 79% with a ΔIc of 140 A at Hext = 500 Oe (coil #2) and a η of 84% with a ΔIc of 125 A at Hext = 530 Oe (coil #3), confirming high rectification values at large supercurrents. The large-current high-efficiency SDE in the coil-shaped SDs will be highly useful for developing the potential field of supercurrent power electronics.

Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.title: Revealing topological protection through unprotected operations in a Majorana parity qubit
Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.authors: Sebastian Miles, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Francesco Zatelli, Nick van Loo, Antonio Lombardi, Vincent P. M. Sietses, Florian J. Bennebroek Evertsz', Bart Roovers, Leo P. Kouwenhoven, Michael Wimmer
Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.abstract: A recent experiment reported coherent parity oscillations between minimal Kitaev chains, demonstrating a Majorana parity qubit (arXiv:2607.09511). Operations on this qubit are controlled by coupling two Kitaev chains and are intrinsically unprotected against noise in the coupling strength. Here we show how the exponential protection in the underlying chains can nevertheless be revealed through unprotected qubit operations. To this end, we develop an analytical theory of quasistatic dephasing for two coupled $N$-site Kitaev chains at the sweet spot. In Rabi experiments, protection can be resolved by adapting the operating point with chain length: depending on the coupling architecture, it appears as an exponentially increasing optimized number of coherent oscillations or as a longer coherence time. Ramsey experiments show an exponentially increasing coherence time, provided the chains can be sufficiently decoupled. Our analytical theory takes into account the non-Gaussian splitting statistics of the Kitaev chains, allowing us to quantitatively predict the scaling with chain length. Moreover, we determine how residual noise and imperfections limit the range of chain lengths over which this scaling can be observed. Our results show how qubit dynamics can be used to probe Majorana protection in experimentally realistic devices.

Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.title: Observation of stacked vortex structure with number controllable Majorana zero mode in Bi$_{2}$Te$_{3}$/FeTe heterojunction
Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.authors: Xinru Han, Zhaokun Luo, Quanxin Hu, Xingjian Zhu, Xiaohong Pan, Dan Mu, Xinyu Liang, Zulin Xu, Qiheng Wang, Ryan L. Kong, Mingyuan Li, Zhengliang Zhang, Fazhi Yang, Mojun Pan, Xin Liu, Qiangqiang Gu, Baiqing Lv, Gan Wang, Hong Ding
Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.abstract: Creation and control of Majorana zero modes (MZMs) in solid devices is the key challenge in realizing fault tolerant topological quantum computation. Here we report spectroscopic evidence for number controllable MZMs in stoichiometric one quintuple layer Bi$_{2}$Te$_{3}$/FeTe heterostructures, together with the observation of stacked vortices in superconducting islands. Low temperature scanning tunnelling microscopy and spectroscopy reveal a long period moire superlattice arising from lattice mismatch, which induces nanoscale modulation of superconducting gaps. Magnetic vortices exhibit a stacked core structure with two layer derived bound state branches: a dispersive branch evolving into an X-shaped pattern away from the vortex center, and a quantum-limit branch characterized by a spatially unsplit MZMs together with discrete integer quantized Caroli-de Gennes-Matricon states. Notably, MZMs are observed in all measured vortices, and their number can be tuned by magnetic field and the size of Bi$_{2}$Te$_{3}$ islands. These results establish stoichiometric 1QL-Bi$_{2}$Te$_{3}$/FeTe as a patterned superconducting interface that enables isolated and few-vortex Majorana configurations, providing a controlled platform for fuse MZMs.

Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.title: Measurement-induced enhancement of the $X$-parity lifetime in a Majorana tetron
Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.authors: Katharina Laubscher, Jay D. Sau, Sankar Das Sarma
Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.abstract: A recent experiment [arXiv:2507.08795] has reported measurements of the interwire $X$-parity lifetime in a Majorana tetron device via the quantum capacitance of an auxiliary readout dot. Motivated by these measurements, we theoretically study the interwire parity lifetime in a minimal model of the coupled dot-tetron system subject to electrostatic noise. We show that coupling to the measurement dot can itself strongly modify the parity dynamics by generating an energy splitting that shifts noise-induced transitions to finite frequency and thereby stabilizes the measured states against low-frequency fluctuations. For representative noise strengths motivated by disordered nanowire devices, we find $X$-parity switching lifetimes of order microseconds in the measurement configuration even when the corresponding bare-tetron coherence time is only tens of nanoseconds long. We analyze both the dispersive regime, where the dot can be integrated out and the dynamics reduces to an effective two-level system, and the near-resonant regime, where all four low-energy states participate. In the latter case, rapid transitions organize the spectrum into two long-lived manifolds that approximately correspond to sectors of the combined dot-tetron $X$-loop parity, yielding effective two-state switching despite the underlying multilevel structure. Our results show that measurement-induced stabilization can substantially enhance the observed $X$-parity switching lifetime, such that the lifetime measured under continuous readout can greatly exceed the intrinsic idle $T_2^*$ coherence time of the isolated Majorana tetron qubit.

Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.title: Topological and kinetic origins of fractional thermal conductance at the topological insulator--superconductor interface
Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.authors: Laurence A. Jacobs, Guillermo R. Zemba
Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.abstract: A recent experiment by Roy et al. (Nat. Commun. 17, 2853 (2026)) demonstrated a robust half-integer thermal conductance plateau, κ_0 T/2, at a bipolar (ν,ν')=(2,-1) junction in bilayer graphene, produced not by non-Abelian topology but by full equilibration of co-propagating electron and hole edge modes. We prove a theorem that fixes when the two origins can be told apart: under full thermal equilibration, the two-terminal thermal conductance of a network of chiral edge segments joined at ideal floating contacts is a rational function of the net chiral central charges of the segments alone, quantities pinned by the gravitational anomaly and invariant under arbitrary local boundary kinetics. The corollary is an impossibility statement: whenever two realizations present the same anomaly data to the same network, no thermal-conductance measurement can distinguish them. That the equilibrated (2,-1) value equals the central charge of a chiral Majorana mode is an arithmetic fact about one filling combination, but wherever such a coincidence occurs it is beyond the reach of thermometry, and the separation must come from the charge sector, which is not anomaly-pinned at a superconducting boundary. We develop the topological insulator-superconductor interface as the application: a vortex carries fractional charge e/4 from the θ= πmagnetoelectric coupling, the boundary hosts a chiral Majorana mode of central charge 1/2, and a laterally adjacent integer quantum Hall (IQH) region supplies the kinetic realization. The Lorenz ratio (anomalous for the isolated Majorana boundary, L_0 / (1 + 4|ν_{IQH}|) in the composite device) and the excess shot noise (growing with B from e/4 vortex tunneling versus locked to IQH plateaus) together resolve the mechanism, provided the quantum Hall edge does not abut the superconductor.

Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.title: Non-Hermitian Statistical Geometry
Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.authors: Xi Hu, Yan-Qiong Ma, Su-Peng Kou
Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.abstract: Particle exchange in two dimensions gives rise to quantum statistics beyond the boson-fermion dichotomy, with central roles in fractional quantum Hall physics, topological quantum computation, and strongly correlated quantum matter. In conventional topological phases, microscopic exchange geometry is compressed into rigid braid and fusion data. We develop a theory of non-Hermitian statistical geometry in which relaxing Hermiticity softens these exchange data into a larger complex space of spectral and relative-geometric degrees of freedom. For two adjacent braid generators, a single projective exchange spectrum is insufficient: their relative eigenline geometry supplies an additional gauge-invariant modulus. On the generic irreducible two-channel branch, braid consistency locks these coordinates through an exact spectrum-geometry relation. Using Riesz projectors and Kato transport, we realize this geometry in a five-arm Kitaev-Majorana network and test spectral and relative-geometric responses in an independent two-dimensional four-vortex Kitaev model. Finite-time dynamics tests the exchange operation, microscopic fusion sewing tests its composition across fusion descriptions, and matched-spectrum controls isolate the role of relative geometry. Nonzero projective Kato curvature shows that braid-consistent, fusion-coherent exchange can depend on the control path. Non-Hermiticity thus exposes exchange geometry, braid consistency re-locks it, fusion coherence further constrains it, and projective flatness determines when geometric exchange becomes intrinsically topological.

Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.title: Search for free non-Abelian anyons in paired composite-fermion states
Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.abstract: The even-denominator fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states, understood as topological superconductors of composite fermions, are predicted to support elementary quasiparticles (QPs) or quasiholes (QHs) obeying non-Abelian braid statistics. Using the microscopic framework of parton theory, we investigate many experimentally observed paired composite-fermion states and find that their elementary QPs and QHs in general bind to form Abelian molecules, thus obscuring non-Abelian braid statistics. An exception is the $ν=1/2$ state in wide quantum wells, where our calculations show free QPs or QHs; we thus identify this state as an especially promising candidate for realizing and studying non-Abelian braid statistics. We also indicate how the study of such bound states can help reveal the topological structure of the state.

Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.title: Equal-Spin local and nonlocal Andreev reflection in altermagnet/superconductor/altermagnet junction
Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.authors: Kai-Yi Lyu, Xing Wang, Yu-Xian Li
Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.abstract: We investigated the equal-spin Andreev reflection phenomenon in an altermagnet/super\-conductor/altermagnet (AM/SC/AM) junction, focusing on the roles of the crystal orientation angle and the Néel vector. The crystal orientation angle in the AM effectively determines the spin-dependent transport channels for both electrons and holes, leading to orientation-dependent local and crossed Andreev reflection in the AM/SC/AM junction. We studied how and under what conditions this equal-spin Andreev reflection occurs. Rotating the Néel vector in the AM substantially increases spin-flip channels for both electrons and holes, giving rise to equal-spin Andreev reflection. When the Néel vector $θ=π/2$, the spin-dependent transmission channels for crystal orientations $α=0$ and $α=π/2$ are completely the same, the Andreev reflection coefficients remain different, reflecting the distinct roles of the Néel vector in spin space and the crystal orientation in real space. By tuning the crystal orientation angle and the Néel vector, orientation-dependent conventional and equal-spin Andreev reflection can be realized. This study reveals that Néel vector rotation is the direct cause of equal-spin Andreev reflection in AM/SC/AM junctions and provides a viable pathway for realizing spin-dependent superconducting transport phenomena in AM heterojunctions.

Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.title: Adiabatic self-vibrations generated by inelastic Andreev tunneling in a movable Cooper-pair box
Interplay between Aharonov-Bohm and Altshuler-Aronov-Spivak oscillations in phase-pure GaAs/InAs core/shell nanowires of different lengths
Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.authors: Farah Basarić, Kaiwen Wang, Tudor-Gabriel Dumitru, Andrei Manolescu, Francisco Alvarado Cesar, Ana M. Sanchez, Christoph Krause, Detlev Grützmacher, Alexander Pawlis, Thomas Schäpers
Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.abstract: In GaAs/InAs core/shell nanowires, comprising a tubular conducting shell, interference phenomena observed under an axial field and originating from closed-loop states encircling the insulating core provide an ideal platform for superconducting quantum devices that utilize effects such as Aharonov-Bohm–type or Altshuler-Aronov-Spivak–type conductance oscillations. Both effects are different in nature with respect to phase rigidity because of interference of non-time-reversed or time-reversed paths, respectively. Since their occurrence is largely governed by averaging effects, which depend on sample dimensions and the transport regime, we present a systematic study of flux-periodic oscillations of phase-pure zinc-blende GaAs/InAs core/shell nanowires as a function of gate voltage for samples with different contact separation lengths. Our analysis shows that with increasing contact separation length, averaging effects result in gradual reduction of h / e -periodic Aharonov-Bohm–type oscillations, while relative to that the h / 2 e -periodic Altshuler-Aronov-Spivak oscillations and its h / 4 e -periodic higher harmonics are enhanced. The additional phase rigidity seen in the h / 3 e -periodic oscillations is attributed to phase rigidity propagating from the neighboring lower harmonics. Our tight-binding transport simulations on nanowires of different lengths which contain only a few scattering centers confirm the experimental observations regarding the different harmonics and their phase rigidity. Together, our experimental and simulation findings indicate quasiballistic transport with persistent Aharonov-Bohm–type and phase-rigid Altshuler-Aronov-Spivak–type oscillations despite few scattering centers.

Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.authors: Mengya Ren, Yaoyao Chen, Yi-Xin Dai, Fudi Zhou, Can Zhang, Zhaoteng Dong, Lili Zhou, Quanzhen Zhang, Huixia Yang, Xiaolong Xu, Yuanxiao Ma, Qing-Feng Sun, Yu Zhang, Yeliang Wang

Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.title: Field-resolved hierarchy of superconducting energy gaps in PdTe
Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.authors: Sangyun Lee, A. M. Donald, D. Duong, S. Huang, R. Gazizulin, C. Huan, Rongying Jin
Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.abstract: Resolving how multiple superconducting energy scales evolve under magnetic field is important for distinguishing multiband, anisotropic, and surface-sensitive superconducting responses. Here, we investigate the superconducting state of PdTe using low-temperature soft point-contact spectroscopy in a sealed $^3$He immersion environment. The resulting Andreev-reflection spectra reveal two characteristic superconducting energy scales near 0.5 and 1.1 meV that are not adequately described by a single-gap BTK model. Both energy scales are progressively suppressed upon warming toward the same superconducting transition temperature $T_c$. In contrast, their magnetic-field evolution reveals two distinct characteristic fields near 4.5 and 7.5 kG. The lower scale is associated with the loss of the zero-resistance superconducting state, whereas the higher-energy spectroscopic response persists to substantially larger fields. Independent field-dependent gap analysis yields suppression scales consistent with those identified from the zero-bias conductance. These results reveal a field-resolved hierarchy of superconducting energy scales in PdTe and indicate superconducting responses with distinct magnetic-field robustness.

Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.title: Electric and Heat Transport in One-Dimensional SNS Junctions with Energy-Dependent Transmission
Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.abstract: We investigate the phase-independent dc components of the electric and heat currents through a one-dimensional superconductor-normal-metal-superconductor (SNS) junction subject to chemical-potential and temperature differences between two superconducting reservoirs. Using a scattering approach based on the Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations, we incorporate multiple Andreev reflections while retaining the energy dependence of transmission through the normal region. We compare energy-independent, quantum-dot-type, and quantum-point-contact transmission profiles. At low bias, both currents exhibit nonlinear features associated with the superconducting gap and multiple Andreev reflections. Their responses to a temperature difference depend remarkably on the transmission profile. At a small finite bias, the electric current depends weakly on the temperature difference for the energy-independent and quantum-dot-type profiles, whereas the quantum-point-contact profile produces a pronounced nonlinear response. The heat current depends nonlinearly on the temperature difference for all three profiles over the parameter range investigated. These results highlight the role of the transmission profile in nonlinear electric and heat transport through SNS junctions and provide a microscopic reference for related transport studies in mesoscopic fermionic superfluid junctions.

Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.title: Emergent gold-induced interfacial magnetism in monolayer FePS$_3$
Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.authors: Giuseppe Buccoliero, Anita Polli, Marli dos Reis Cantarino, Rachel Nickel, Aloïs Arrighi, Roberto Sant, Tristan Riccardi, Valérie Reita, Nedjma Bendiab, Laëtitia Marty, Kurt Kummer, Johann Coraux, Nicholas B. Brookes
Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.abstract: Owing to their atomically clean interfaces and extreme thinness, two-dimensional (2D) materials are ideal hosts for strong proximity effects, whereby contact with an adjacent material reshapes their ground state. Here, we demonstrate such an effect within a hybrid heterostructure, between the 2D antiferromagnet FePS$_3$ and an ultrathin gold film. Rather than a passive support, the latter profoundly changes the nature of the magnetism in the 2D magnet, inducing a sizeable interfacial moment. Large-area flakes from Au-assisted exfoliation, combined with element-selective X-ray absorption mapping, enable a layer-by-layer study from monolayer to bulk, benchmarked against an inert SiO$_2$ substrate reference. At 9 T and 5 K, the monolayer on gold shows a three-fold enhanced X-ray magnetic circular dichroism relative to SiO$_2$, with a $\sim$40% reduction of the orbital-to-spin moment ratio. Resonant inelastic X-ray scattering reveals a collapse of the crystal-field (d-d) excitations and a massive spectral-weight transfer to the charge-transfer region, unveiling the microscopic mechanism behind this change. Supported by atomic multiplet calculations, we identify interfacial charge transfer and Fe 3d-Au hybridization as the origin of these effects, which decay over the first three layers and vanish at the pentalayer, establishing layer number combined with substrate engineering as an atomically precise handle.

Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.title: Long-range spin-polarized Josephson effect in ballistic S/F/S junctions with precessing magnetization
Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.authors: E. S. Andriyakhina, M. Mansouri, M. Breitkreiz, P. W. Brouwer
Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.abstract: We present a theory of ballistic N/F/S and S/F/S junctions with a uniformly precessing magnetization, which generates long-range equal-spin superconducting correlations [Takahashi , , Houzet, ]. The nonequilibrium distribution of Andreev bound states leads to a strongly nonsinusoidal current-phase relationship for large precession angles. We derive detailed results for ballistic junctions involving partially and fully polarized ferromagnets. In the fully polarized half-metal limit, the magnetization precession switches the junction from an “off” state with vanishing subgap current to an “on” state with finite Andreev conductance and finite Josephson current.

Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.title: A Bispecific Nanobridge Derived from Immunogenic Tumor Membranes Restores Dendritic Cell–T Cell Crosstalk for Enhanced Solid Tumor Immunotherapy
Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.authors: Xueqian Li, Lei Qiao, Wanrong Wang, Yan Xiong, Le Zhang, Guisong Shan, Qiuting Sun, Tao Ding, Xiaoyan He
Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.abstract: Abstract In solid tumors, communication between dendritic cells (DCs) and T cells is impaired by poor immune infiltration and lack of physical contact, limiting current immunotherapies. Here, we develop a bispecific immune-bridging platform (NVMB) to address these limitations. NVMB consists of tumor cell membrane-derived nanovesicles enriched with damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) that activate DCs and support T-cell responses. The vesicle surface is further functionalized with two aptamers targeting DCs and CD8+ T cells, respectively, thereby enhancing their spatial proximity and facilitating functional DC–T cell interactions. This biomimetic design combines colloidal stability with programmable surface functionalization. Mechanistically, NVMB promotes DC–T interactions and enhances activation-associated phenotypes in both cell populations. In multiple immunocompetent mouse tumor models, NVMB suppresses tumor growth, increases intratumoral accumulation of mature DCs and activated CD8+ T cells, and reshapes the tumor microenvironment transcriptome toward enhanced antitumor immune responses. Moreover, combination with immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) further improves antitumor efficacy compared with either monotherapy, supporting the potential of NVMB as a complementary strategy for enhancing ICB responses. In patient-derived cocultures of circulating tumor cells (CTCs) and autologous peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), NVMB enhances T-cell-mediated clearance of CTCs. These findings support NVMB as a stable and modular nanoplatform that integrates immunogenic signaling with immune-cell spatial coordination, providing a promising strategy for strengthening antitumor immunity and improving the efficacy of existing immunotherapies.

Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.title: The WorkReach model for urban work location choices through economic complexity and informality
Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.authors: Ollin D. Langle-Chimal, Steffen Knoblauch, Marta C. González
Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.abstract: Abstract Human mobility in urban areas largely depends on the spatial distribution of jobs and who pursues them, yet how workers balance proximity against economic opportunity remains poorly understood. Existing mechanistic models capture physically interpretable effects such as distance decay, but overlook how socioeconomic factors shape commuting decisions. We present WorkReach, a model grounded in discrete choice theory that embeds informality and economic complexity into a utility function and represents commuting as the outcome of workers behaving as if maximizing it. Applied to four cities in the United States, Mexico, and Brazil, it reproduces commuting flows as accurately as widely used benchmarks while making the underlying choices interpretable. Here, we show that workers consistently commute farther to economically sophisticated areas, while the role of informality differs across regions, and that measuring accessibility by the perceived benefit of opportunities, not just physical proximity, highlights disparities conventional metrics overlook.

Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.title: Emergent Phenomena in Wurtzite Ferroelectric Semiconductors
Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.authors: Haoze Zhang, Alexei Gruverman, Pankaj Sharma
Majorana SC-Semiconductor Hybrids.abstract: Abstract The emergence of ferroelectricity in wurtzite-structured semiconducting materials broadens the material landscape beyond traditional perovskites, introducing design rules for scalable nanoelectronic devices with an inherent thermal robustness. These materials combine large spontaneous polarization, ultrathin scalability, and compatibility with back-end-of-line processing. This review discusses the state-of-the-art and recent progress in understanding their ferroelectric behavior, from atomic-scale switching pathways and proximity-triggered, electrically controlled polarization states to charged yet intrinsically stable domain walls. Progress in compositional tuning, strain and interface engineering, heterostructure design, and advanced synthesis strategies is highlighted, including key material and device challenges for the integration of wurtzite ferroelectrics into next-generation memory, logic-in-memory, and neuromorphic computing systems.

NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.title: Molecule-intercalated van der Waals Josephson junctions uncover complex multiband superconductivity
NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.authors: Daniel Margineda, David Caldevilla-Asenjo, Covadonga Álvarez-García, Daniel Tezze, Raul Arenal, Maxim Ilyn, Celia Rogero, Luis E. Hueso, Marco Gobbi
NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.abstract: Intercalation of molecular species provides a route to tailor the electronic structure in van der Waals superconductors, yet intercalated compounds have rarely been integrated into phase-sensitive quantum devices. Here, we realize hybrid molecular Josephson junctions based on TaS2/NbSe2 heterostructures. Selective intercalation of the TaS2 electrode induces monolayer-like Ising superconductivity, while the junctions exhibit asymmetric Fraunhofer interference, field-induced and spontaneous Josephson diode effects. The zero-field diode disappears upon reversing the electrode stacking and re-emerges after intercalating the lower NbSe2 electrode. These findings indicate that the hybrid superconducting electrode hosts unconventional superconductivity underlying the nonreciprocal transport, while molecular intercalation acts as a tuning knob for its internal phase structure. This behavior is consistent with a time-reversal-symmetry-breaking multiband superconducting state characterized by a nontrivial relative phase between superconducting condensates. Our results establish hybrid molecular Josephson junctions as a quantum-device platform for phase-sensitive investigation and integration of molecularly engineered superconductors, opening opportunities to uncover and engineer unconventional superconducting phases.

NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.title: Chemical-Potential-Dependent Superconducting Spectroscopy on Bi2Te3/NbSe2 Heterostructures
NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.authors: Pengyu Hu, Chun Yu Wan, Qiaoyan Yu, Chen Qian, Yisheng Gu, Xian Du, Xuhui Ning, Tingwen Miao, Shi Chen, Zihao Ma, Hao Yang, Hemian Yi, Weijiong Chen, Xiaoxue Liu, Liang Liu, Dandan Guan, Yaoyi Li, Shiyong Wang, Canhua Liu, Sangen Zhao, Fulin Wang, Junwei Liu, Hao Zheng, Jinfeng Jia
NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.abstract: High-resolution scanning tunneling spectroscopy performed at dilution refrigerator temperatures was employed to investigate the superconducting properties of topological insulator/superconductor (Bi2Te3/NbSe2) heterostructures. Coherence peaks with inner kinks or inner peaks, deviating from the conventional single s-wave spectral line shape, were observed in both 5 quintuple-layer (5QL) and 7QL Bi2Te3 thin films. Based on the combination of chemical-potential-dependent spectroscopic measurements and model simulations, we conclude that these spectral features arise from contributions of bulk and surface states in Bi2Te3 by selectively proximity-coupled to a single superconducting gap from NbSe2, rather than inheriting the complicated superconductor's order parameter of NbSe2.

NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.title: Robust skyrmion nucleation and transport via composition gradient in rare earth-transition metal ferrimagnets
NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.authors: Pietro Diona, Luca Maranzana, Sergey Artyukhin
NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.abstract: Magnetic skyrmions are typically nucleated via localized excitation methods, such as laser heating, spin-orbit torques, or engineered defects, and their controlled transport is often limited by the skyrmion Hall effect. Here, we demonstrate that spatial gradients in rare-earth--transition-metal alloys, achievable through patterned laser writing, enable both deterministic nucleation and controlled transport. The strategy leverages engineered compositional gradient to cross the magnetization compensation point, defining regions with opposite magnetization. An out-of-plane magnetic field selectively reverses the magnetization, generating a skyrmion. Crucially, the same compositional design enables a channel tuned to the spin angular momentum compensation point, where skyrmions are driven by spin-orbit torques at high velocity with vanishing skyrmion Hall effect. Local composition variations act as pinning sites, enabling threshold-controlled trapping and release.

NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.title: Resolving the interfacial mechanical landscape of monolayer NbSe2 grown by confined epitaxy
NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.authors: Ye Wang
NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.abstract: Confined epitaxy has recently emerged as a novel methodology for controlled growth of high-quality monolayer two-dimensional (2D) materials. However, mechanistic understanding remains limited to analysing nucleus adsorption and diffusion barriers. Here, I discover that van der Waals (vdW) confinement not only affects the specific adsorption and diffusion of nuclei on confined substrates but also induces strong coupling to atomic forces at the interface. Using artificial intelligence (AI) assisted density functional theory (DFT) calculations, I study how vdW confinement couples to the atomic motion of monolayer NbSe2 grown between c-plane sapphire and hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN). The calculated force-electronic landscape yields large mechanical forces of +0.070 and -0.04 eV per Angstrom on Nb and Se, respectively, giving rise to a unit-cell interfacial interaction energy up to 2.4 eV, comparable to reported adsorption and diffusion energies on similar substrates. The results indicate that interfacial mechanics may explain the success of confined epitaxy. The findings suggest that tuning interfacial mechanics, and related vdW mechanochemistry, could be a promising route to high-throughput, high-quality materials synthesis.

NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.title: Dynamics of Charge-Density-Wave Puddles in 2 H -NbSe2
NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.authors: Shreya Kumbhakar, Marina Esposito, Anjan Kumar N M, Liwen Feng, Tommaso Confalone, Vasilisa Gerega, Flavia Lo Sardo, Rafiqul Alam, Davide Masarotti, Francesco Tafuri, Thomas Böhm, Mahmoud Abdel-Hafiez, Sushmita Chandra, Claudia Felser, Kornelius Nielsch, Nicola Poccia, Stefan Kaiser, Golam Haider
NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.abstract: Abstract Electronic phases in quantum materials are often governed by nanoscale inhomogeneity, where local order develops within spatially confined regions, or puddles. A prominent example is an incommensurate charge-density-wave (I-CDW) comprising locally commensurate domains. In 2H-NbSe2, such an I-CDW state persists alongside lattice anharmonicity and superconductivity, raising fundamental questions about the dynamical stabilization of CDW order in puddles. Here, using Raman scattering, we reveal a strong Fano-coupling between interlayer shear phonons and the CDW amplitude mode. Our time-resolved reflectivity measurement shows a low-frequency ∼0.2 THz coherent overdamped oscillation onsetting within the CDW regime at ∼17K, indicating a previously unexplored transition. This we identify as a Fano-coupled phonon-CDW hybrid emerging from the collective dynamics of CDW puddles. We establish an overdamped-oscillator framework for capturing such intertwined glassy dynamics. These results highlight how lattice pinning and electronic correlations shape CDW order in layered materials, insight crucial for designing novel van der Waals devices.

NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.title: Giant geometric nonlinear transport in inhomogeneously strained Bi$_2$Se$_3$ single crystalline slabs
NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.authors: Igor Veremchuk, Pavlo Makushko, Anita Guarino, Muhammad Waqee Ur Rehman, Rosalba Tatiana Fittipaldi, Tobias Kosub, Alexej Pashkin, Fabian Ganss, Oleg A. Petrenko, Proloy T. Das, Rui Xu, Rhonald Burgos Atencia, Debottam Mandal, Antonio Vecchione, Carmine Ortix, Denys Makarov
NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.abstract: Electrical transport in non-centrosymmetric materials exhibits a nonlinear conductivity tensor component that generates second-harmonic voltages in response to applied electric fields. Harnessing this effect is essential for developing zero-threshold electromagnetic energy harvesters and broadband frequency upconverters, both of which require maximizing the nonlinear responsivity. Here, we demonstrate that inhomogeneously strained macroscopic slabs of the topological insulator Bi$_2$Se$_3$ achieve a record-high nonlinear responsivity of $10^4\,μ$m/V: a six orders of magnitude boost compared to its thin-film counterparts. We attribute this giant enhancement to a classical geometric nonlinear transport effect, which is driven by complex strain gradients within the bulk material. Notably, a similar geometric mechanism known as geometric nonlinear Hall was previously observed only in microscale-patterned structures. Our findings establish macroscopic strain engineering as a powerful route to enhance nonlinear transport, with immediate relevance to a broad class of layered systems, including transition metal dichalcogenides and moiré heterostructures.

NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.title: Graphene-Confined Growth of Few-Layer PtSe2 via One-Step Selenization
NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.authors: Timea Ema Krajčovičová, Peter Kotrusz, Viera Skákalová, Agáta Laurenčíková, Igor Píš, Martin Hulman, Kimmo Mustonen, Michaela Sojková
NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.abstract: Platinum diselenide (PtSe$_2$), a member of the transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) family, is a promising material for next-generation electronic and optoelectronic applications due to its thickness-dependent properties, transitioning from semimetallic in bulk to semiconducting behavior at the few-layer limit. However, the scalable fabrication of large-area ultrathin PtSe$_2$ films remains challenging, as conventional selenization of pre-deposited Pt layers often leads to undesired three-dimensional clustered growth. This work explores a novel strategy for promoting two-dimensional growth of PtSe$_2$ by employing a graphene-mediated confinement approach. The method involves coating a Pt layer with graphene oxide (GO), followed by annealing in a selenium atmosphere, which results in the simultaneous formation of PtSe$_2$ and the reduction of GO to graphene. The graphene overlayer acts as a physical confinement layer, suppressing vertical growth and enabling the synthesis of graphene-confined PtSe$_2$ heterostructures on centimetre-scale substrates and promoting lateral connectivity of PtSe$_2$ regions observed by STEM. Scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), including temperature-resolved in situ atomic-resolution measurements, was used to investigate the influence of selenization temperature on the growth mechanism and structural evolution of PtSe$_2$ films. The results show that graphene confinement stabilizes lateral growth and promotes the formation of few-layer films with improved structural ordering. Beyond PtSe$_2$, this graphene-assisted approach provides a general strategy for fabricating and stabilizing ultrathin TMD layers, including those prone to environmental degradation, providing a new outlook for enabling detailed studies of their intrinsic properties.

NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.title: Phononic Frequency Combs in Twisted Bilayer Transition Metal Dichalcogenide Heterostructures from First Principles
NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.authors: Naman Arora, Adarsh Ganesan
NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.abstract: Phononic frequency combs are equidistant spectral ladders generated when a driven vibrational mode transfers energy to an autoparametrically excited subharmonic mode through anharmonic intermode coupling. In previous studies, the coupling strength governing this energy transfer has typically been treated as a free parameter, extracted from a fabricated device, or adopted from an earlier calculation for a specific mode pair. As a result, whether a given crystal can support a phononic frequency comb, and the drive strength required to generate it, has not been predictable a priori. Here we obtain the complete parameter set from density functional theory. Twisted bilayers of \MoSSe{} and \MoSMoSe{} at the commensurate angle $21.787^{\circ}$ adopt space group $P3$ in a 42-atom \rootseven{} moiré supercell. The second-order force constants provide the mode frequencies; the third-order constants provide the linewidths through the Boltzmann transport equation and hence the quality factors; and the same third-order tensor projected onto the phonon eigenvectors of a chosen mode pair provides the anharmonic couplings $\kt$ and $\kss$. Both bilayers constitute a mode pair within $0.8\%$ of the $2\!:\!1$ resonance with $ω_1/ω_2 = 1.9923$ in \MoSSe{} and $1.9943$ in \MoSMoSe{}. By integrating the resulting two-mode equations, both modes generate combs through a discontinuous transition: at $701\,\fth$ in \MoSSe{} the envelope variance rises from $2.1\times10^{3}$ to $1.37\times10^{4}$ and the tooth count of mode 1 from 7 to 16 within a single $5\,\fth$ increment, identifying the onset as subcritical. The spectral entropy peaks \emph{before} this jump, at $341\,\fth$. The two compounds carry comparable coupling, differing by a factor of $1.2$. However, the comb excitation threshold is set by the quality-factors of signal modes: $Q_2 = 672$ for \MoSSe{} and $Q_2 = 3844$ for \MoSMoSe{}.

NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.title: Direct view of exciton and carrier dynamics in twisted bilayer graphene
NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.authors: Gianmarco Gatti, Anders S. Mortensen, Zhihao Jiang, Alfred J. H. Jones, Gesa-R. Siemann, Thomas S. Nielsen, Søren Ulstrup, Naina Kushwaha, Bruce Weaver, Yu Zhang, Emma Springate, Charlotte E. Sanders, Vibha Reddy, Ulrich Starke, Philip Hofmann
NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.abstract: Twisted bilayer graphene (tBLG) on H-intercalated SiC (twist angle of $9 \pm 1^{\circ}$) is studied by position\mbox{-}, time\mbox{-}, and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES). Both graphene layers are hole doped, with a Dirac-point offset of 30~meV. Time-resolved ARPES near the van Hove singularity reveals a spectral feature within the hybridization-induced band gap, together with excited electrons in the conduction band. The in-gap feature exhibits distinct dynamics, and its binding energy and $k$-space location are consistent with the proposed non-hydrogenic ``ghost-Fano'' exciton arising from destructive interference between two nearly degenerate excitonic channels. Near the Dirac points, the twist separates the largely layer-polarized Dirac cones in momentum space, providing direct layer selectivity. We find markedly different peak electronic temperatures in the two graphene layers, even though their subsequent cooling dynamics are very similar. We attribute this to an ultrafast interlayer redistribution of electronic energy, driven by an interlayer electric field that arises from the different doping in the layers.

NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.title: High-mobility spin transport mediated by indirect excitons in a van der Waals heterostructure
NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.authors: Zhiwen Zhou, W. J. Brunner, Luc M. Nguyen, C. A. Lozano, G. Mercado, L. H. Fowler-Gerace, L. V. Butov
NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.abstract: Efficient spin transport with high spin mobility is of both fundamental and practical significance for spintronics. Spin can be transferred by moving particles. However, particle scattering limits spin transfer and prevents high spin mobilities. In this work, we study the kinetics of spin transport mediated by a quantum system of indirect excitons (IXs) in a van der Waals heterostructure composed of atomically thin transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs). This spin transfer mechanism allows for the realization of efficient spin transport characterized by a high spin mobility reaching 10$^5$ cm$^2$/(eV$\cdot$s), which is orders of magnitude higher than that achieved via standard diffusive spin transport in TMD materials. The suppression of IX scattering enables high-mobility spin transport.

NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.title: Evidence of an anisotropic Griffiths phase in a two-dimensional van der Waals magnet
NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.authors: Anupam K. Singh, Dhananjay Nair, Holger Meyerheim, Stuart S. P. Parkin, Banabir Pal
NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.abstract: Over the last decade, the emerging field of two-dimensional van der Waals magnetism has focused mainly on long-range-ordered magnetic phases. Disordered magnetic phases, however, remain largely unexplored. Here, we report a highly anisotropic Griffiths phase driven by self-intercalation in the van der Waals magnet Fe5GeTe2. We find evidence of short-range-ordered ferromagnetic clusters embedded in a paramagnetic matrix, which dominate the magnetic response between the Curie temperature and a higher characteristic Griffiths temperature. An anomalous power-law divergence in the magnetic susceptibility, universal Lee Yang scaling, and distinct entropy anomalies provide further evidence for this phase. Strikingly, the non-analytic Griffiths response emerges exclusively under in-plane magnetic fields, whereas out-of-plane fields abruptly alter this behavior. This directional dependence indicates that the local magnetic interactions within nanoscale clusters are closely coupled to the layered lattice geometry. Our findings establish a regime of dimensionally constrained, disorder-driven magnetism and identify self-intercalated van der Waals magnets as a platform for investigating the interplay between magnetic disorder, anisotropy, and reduced dimensionality.

NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.title: Light-induced interlayer spacing dynamics via orbital phonon coupling
NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.authors: Wenwen Mao, Hanbyul Kim, Angel Rubio, Dongbin Shin
NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.abstract: Interlayer coupling controls the electronic properties of layered van der Waals transition metal dichalcogenides. We investigate light-induced control of the interlayer spacing through orbital-selective excitation in trilayer 1T'-WSe2 and 1T'-WS2. Real-time time-dependent density functional theory simulations show that the interlayer spacing contracts or expands depending on whether chalcogen p-orbital density is depleted from or accumulated in the interlayer region. Effective Lindblad models coupled to the lattice dynamics reproduce these contrasting responses with simplified dynamics. A single effective excited state captures the cosine-like displacive motion in trilayer 1T'-WSe2, whereas the shift of the equilibrium spacing in trilayer 1T'-WS2 requires two excited states with different electron-phonon couplings and relaxation channels. Static calculations at varied interlayer spacings indicate that these spacing changes modify the electronic gaps and could access different electronic phases. These results connect orbital redistribution, carrier relaxation, and interlayer breathing motion, and establish orbital-selective optical excitation as a route to tuning the electronic properties of layered materials.

NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.title: Bond-Switching Reconstruction in Bare Ti3C2 MXene
NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.authors: Kui Lin
NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.abstract: MXene properties are typically tuned through composition, surface termination, and intercalation, while the metal-carbon framework topology is considered fixed. Here, we demonstrate that this framework can reconstruct. Unconstrained relaxations of biaxially strained bare Ti3C2 yield a dynamically stable polymorph, N, featuring a 15-atom primitive cell, six distinct Ti-C bond classes, and 2.55 Å Ti-Ti pairs. The coherent transformation pathway crosses an 8.47 eV barrier per cell but first reaches another reconstructed minimum, N', lying 1.08 eV below N, revealing a family of bond-switched networks. Phase N lies 7.58 eV per cell above the parent. Reverse barriers along the calculated pathway are 1.50 and 1.98 eV per cell for N and N', respectively. Reconstruction quenches the parent spin polarization, yielding a nonmagnetic metal with a nearly fourfold increase in Fermi-level density of states. Bader and electron-localization analyses suggest charge redistribution from C toward Ti associated with Ti-Ti pairing. In multilayers, reconstructed layers form interlayer Ti-C bonds. A 10% biaxial tension halves the phase-energy difference, and pressure reverses phase ordering near 85 GPa. These results establish bond-switching reconstruction as a mechanically controllable structural degree of freedom in MXenes.

NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.title: Phase-dependent electronic structure of two-dimensional Ag layers at the graphene/SiC interface
NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.authors: Sawani Datta, Boyang Zheng, Arpit Jain, Kathrin Küster, Joshua A. Robinson, Vincent H. Crespi, Ulrich Starke
NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.abstract: Intercalation at the graphene/SiC interface provides a controlled route to stabilize atomically thin layers with properties distinct from their bulk counterparts. In this platform, the structure and stability of the intercalated phase depend sensitively on the defect landscape of the starting substrate. For intercalated two-dimensional silver at the graphene/SiC interface, two phases have been observed: a phase epitaxial to the SiC lattice, called Ag ( 1 ) , readily obtained following the conventional intercalation method under ultra-high-vacuum conditions and extensively characterized, and a more densely packed phase, called Ag ( 2 ) , which has remained largely unexplored. Here we report an ultra-high-vacuum preparation method of the second phase intercalated at the graphene/SiC interface; this phase was previously prepared via high-pressure confinement heteroepitaxy. Low-energy electron diffraction shows that Ag ( 2 ) is rotated by 30 ∘ relative to the SiC lattice and forms supercells, in contrast to the ( 1 × 1 ) epitaxial relation of Ag ( 1 ) with SiC. High-resolution angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy reveals a more complex Ag ( 2 ) band dispersion compared to Ag ( 1 ) , as a consequence of the modified Ag-Si interaction in the denser phase. In density functional theory calculations, by defining the unfolding entropy, which, in a quantified way, finds that the band structure of Ag ( 2 ) is more suitable to be unfolded to the SiC primitive cell, the resulting unfolded band dispersion is in great agreement with the experimental data. We further show that the different intercalated Ag phases tune the electronic properties of the overlying quasi-free-standing graphene layer differently: compared with Ag ( 1 ) , Ag ( 2 ) yields an ∼ 1.75 times higher charge carrier density and modifies the charge-plasmon interaction of the graphene layer, indicating a change in effective screening at the interface.

NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.title: From Micro to Nano: Boosting γ-MnO2 Cathode Performance through Particle Size Engineering
NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.authors: Ella Davidi, Isaac Loke, Samuel Eisenberg, Xinzhe Xue, Megan C. Freyman, Asya Orhan, Erika P. Ramos, Jianchao Ye, Seongkoo Cho, Makena White, Christopher Nelson, Hanyu Wang, Christine A. Orme, Bruce Dunn, Marcus A. Worsley, Yat Li
NbSe2 and Intercalated TMDs.abstract: Abstract Fast-charging lithium-ion batteries require cathodes that sustain rapid Li+ transport while maintaining structural and interfacial stability. Here, we investigate particle-size effects in γ-MnO2 by comparing micron-sized (4.4 ± 0.8 μm) and nanosized (62 ± 21 nm) particles under identical conditions. Nanosized γ-MnO2 delivers 160.1 mAh g–1 at C/10 and retains ∼66% capacity at 5C while exhibiting lower charge-transfer and diffusion-related impedance. Cyclic voltammetry and Dunn’s analysis reveal a 68.9% capacitive contribution at 2 mV s–1, indicating a shift toward faster surface-controlled charge storage enabled by increased surface area and shorter Li+ diffusion pathways. GITT measurements show deeper lithiation (x ≈ 0.65 vs 0.48 in LixMnO2) and a more homogeneous solid-solution-like intercalation regime in nanosized particles, avoiding bulk phase-transition kinetic bottlenecks. The nanosized cathode retains 70% capacity with ∼99.5% Coulombic efficiency after 400 cycles at 3C, demonstrating particle-size engineering as an effective strategy for high-rate, long-life advanced battery energy storage.

Quantum Materials Transport.title: Enhancement of the Topological Hall Effect through Engineering the Skyrmion Size and Shape
Quantum Materials Transport.authors: Kazuma Murata, Ryunosuke Terasawa, Hiroaki Ishizuka
Quantum Materials Transport.abstract: The topological Hall effect of skyrmions is a promising electrical probe of magnetic textures, but its small magnitude limits applications. In this work, we theoretically investigate the topological Hall effect induced by sparsely distributed skyrmions in the weak-coupling limit, focusing on how the size and shape of the skyrmion affect the Hall effect. To this end, we used a formalism based on angular-momentum eigenstates, which enables systematic analysis within reasonable computation time. We found that, in clean materials where the electron mean-free path is comparable to or larger than the skyrmion size, the Hall effect depends considerably on the size and shape of the skyrmion. In particular, the Hall effect is largest when $k_Fλ\sim 1$, and its magnitude can be tuned by the domain-wall width of skyrmions. These findings provide a basis for investigating how the shape and size of skyrmions affect transport properties and demonstrate that the topological Hall effect is controllable by engineering these properties.
